title: DFI ARH171/ARH173 Spans Two Core Ultra Generations on One Mini-ITX Design
dek: DFI’s ARH171/ARH173 puts Meteor Lake and Arrow Lake Core Ultra options on one Mini-ITX platform, giving OEMs a way to vary performance tiers without requalifying an entirely different board.
summary: The key design signal is lifecycle flexibility: DFI is using one board architecture to cover two Core Ultra generations and a broad performance range, which can reduce requalification work across product tiers.
whyItMatters: DFI lists 16 processor options across Meteor Lake-U/H and Arrow Lake-U/H, spanning roughly 15–28W.
Arrow Lake-H configurations are cited at up to 99 TOPS using integrated CPU, GPU and NPU resources.
A common board can reduce mechanical and validation churn when an OEM needs several product tiers or a processor migration path.

reporting.heading: One board can be a lifecycle strategy
paragraphs: The ARH171/ARH173 is designed around a single Mini-ITX architecture that accepts two Intel Core Ultra generations. DFI positions this as a way to qualify one platform and then choose processor performance, price and lifecycle per product tier.
For OEMs, that can be more valuable than maximizing a benchmark because board requalification, enclosure changes and peripheral validation are expensive.

reporting.heading: The platform covers a wide AI and thermal range
paragraphs: DFI lists 15W and 28W processor options and up to 99 TOPS for Arrow Lake-H configurations, with integrated Arc graphics and an NPU. The board also supports up to three 2.5GbE ports and four displays.
That gives system designers room to use the same mechanical platform for comparatively light HMI or vision tasks and more demanding analytics systems.

reporting.heading: Modular I/O reduces custom-board pressure
paragraphs: DFI’s M.2 A-key expansion can add display, cellular, USB, MIPI-camera or capture functions depending on the module.
The remaining questions are SKU-specific AI performance, thermals, long-term processor availability and the exact expansion combinations supported in production.

flypigTake: ARH171/ARH173 is a good example of design intelligence being about lifecycle as much as compute. A common board across two processor generations can reduce requalification cost, particularly for OEMs shipping several edge-system tiers.
